column1: # Spec tests that flake, so `bun run test:neo-spec --ci` never judges them, in either direction, on
# any platform: the job summary shows each one's outcome on every run, and none is on an expected
# list. Edit this file by hand in a pull request; no command adds or removes an entry. Each entry
# says why the test flakes and where its fix is tracked. Take it off when the fix lands.

column4: Linux only (macOS runs the whole test in about 1.4 s), and slow rather than stuck. From the test's second or third step on, every mouse action on Linux takes about 1 s after Neo sends its input (each hover and each #close click about 990 ms; under 200 ms in the first step, and throughout on macOS), while resolving, actionability, scrolling and the stable wait take about 20 ms. The nine steps then take 26-31 s against the 30 s test timeout, so it times out in the last step (hide 1 times) at whatever it is doing then: the hover, the handler's #close click, the #target click, or the wait for the interstitial to hide. Since the gate's own pull request (first failure 4960909e9, run 43163445473, before #3501 and #3502) it timed out in 67 of 71 full runs; alone it passed 23 of 45 reruns, so a job goes red when both reruns time out (43164693735, 43196514344, 43236661656), and it went red when it happened to pass while listed as failing (43183791832, 43189312372). Not known: what each input waits about 1 s for (Input.dispatchMouseEvent's reply or Neo's hit-target verdict; the trace does not split them), or why the wait starts a few actions in.
column5: No task yet. Unconfirmed: it may share SS-054's cause, a tab that stops producing frames on Linux. Neo's launch passes none of Playwright's --disable-renderer-backgrounding, --disable-background-timer-throttling or --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows; that is untested.

column3: page screenshot animations › should not capture css animations in shadow DOM
column4: Linux only (macOS passes every verifier run): Chromium never replies to Neo's Page.captureScreenshot for the test's tab, so a screenshot times out at 30 s; never a size or pixel difference. In each attempt the first capture takes ~40 ms, the second ~3.4 s, the third gets no reply until teardown (SS-024 and SS-052 stall the same way). Not load: it fails alone and at 8 light workers. Not Linux rendering: vanilla Playwright on the same browser and runner passes 12 of 12. Not fonts: that wait ends in 0-1 ms. No step of Neo's screenshot or page setup was found to cause it: switching off the pointer hide, the document watch, or Accessibility/DOM/chooser setup, and adding a clip, tab activation, a normal window state, viewport emulation, Runtime or Network, each left it timing out; switching off preparation and the fonts wait made SS-054 fail early on the still-running animation instead (inconclusive for it), while SS-024 and SS-052 kept stalling without preparation (diagnostic runs 43207466426, 43209303746, 43210965696, 43213221242, 43215826260, 43217512979 on branch diag/ss054-fonts). The test cancels its only animation before each capture, so a capture waits on a frame something else must cause: that is why it passes sometimes, and why an isolated-world getComputedStyle override changed it.
column5: No task yet. Unconfirmed: the one difference from Playwright left untested is how the tab is made and held, which would put it outside the SDK: core opens agent tabs natively (BrowserOS Browser.createTab, in the background of the default profile's window, with focus emulation), Playwright's pages come from Target.createTarget in their own context and window. That is browseros-core or BrowserOS. The listed SS-027, SS-053, SS-057, SS-059 and SS-065 are likely the same stall.
